prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a passenger and reported knee injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1072; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was stopped at a red light in the left lane of the roadway in Pasadena, Texas, when the rear of the vehicle was struck by Driver 2, whose vehicle was traveling behind at a speed the responding officer judged too close for conditions. Driver 1 confirmed the collision occurred as described, and Driver 2 acknowledged the impact. Two independent witnesses on the adjacent sidewalk gave statements consistent with the sequence of events, and scene photographs were taken. The damage to the rear bumper and trunk area of Driver 1's vehicle is consistent with the reported force of the impact. Passenger was seated in the front passenger seat at the time, and both the officer and the witnesses confirmed Passenger's presence in the vehicle. Passenger reported pain in the left knee at the scene and was evaluated by medical personnel, but it is not yet clear whether the injury resulted from this crash. No prior damage to the vehicle is known to the officer or to Driver 1. Driver 1 was identified as the named insured on the policy covering the vehicle, and no citations were issued pending further review.
